title: Heather Gaudio Fine Art opens The Late Summer Show featuring three contemporary artists
summary: Heather Gaudio Fine Art is presenting The Late Summer Show, a three-person exhibition featuring new works by Sophie Kitching, Jae Ko and Matthew Shlian. The show dates are August 22nd -October 3rd. Exhibiting for the first time at the gallery, Sophie Kitching is presenting new paintings from the “Invisible Green” series, among others. The French-British artist directs her multi-media practice around architecture, nature and the environment, inspired by found objects, color and form. In her captivating botanical landscapes sourced from memory, decorative patterns and nature, space plays an equally important part as the depicted motifs, allowing the viewer to navigate their eye between and through prismatic gestural flora, fauna and ensuing drips. title: Georgia Museum of Art publishes first monograph on sculptor Harold Rittenberry Jr.
summary: At the core of artist Harold Rittenberry Jr.’s work is a deep love for nature. Many of his sculptures celebrate local culture or commemorate historic events. Others reflect his interior world, an imaginative realm where animals of the African savanna coexist with mythological creatures like mermaids, unicorns and fauns. His steel silhouettes frequently include simple messages that gently remind us to center hope, joy, peace, care and his greatest insight, “love is all,” within our lives. Born on Christmas Day in 1938, Rittenberry has spent most of his life in Athens, Georgia. He taught himself to weld intricate silhouettes into steel and made his sculptures accessible to all. Long before collectors around the world took notice of his talent, Rittenberry turned the heads of passerby by transforming the front lawn of his home into his “Spirit Yard,” an ever-changing menagerie of his latest creations. title: Landmarks announces Floating Landscape, a major new work by Maya Lin
summary: Landmarks, the public art program of The University of Texas at Austin, announces a major new work by Maya Lin, one of the most influential artists of the last half‑century. Titled Floating Landscape, the 3,600-square-foot-structure extends Lin’s ongoing investigation of landscape, memory, and the built environment. It represents the artist’s first work of public art in Texas and first commission in the state. Landmarks will celebrate the opening of the project on April 9, 2027, hosting a public conversation between Lin and Jana La Brasca, an art historian and curatorial contributor for the project. Additional details will be available in the coming months. Lin is known for her groundbreaking, large-scale environmental artworks that establish unique connections to the land. title: The right moves: Decades of dance curated from the Life archive
summary: When publisher Henry R. Luce founded Life magazine in 1936, its aim was: “To see life; to see the world; to eyewitness great events.” Life dedicated its sixth issue to the world of dance, recognizing its importance, not just as a source of joy, but as an expression of community and culture. From Vegas to Hollywood sound stages, from Paris nightclubs to Woodstock, from the Western Provinces of China to Harlem ballrooms, Let’s Dance showcases the evolution and impact of dance, as captured by Life photographers, from the late 1930s to the early 1970s. Featuring over 200 mainly unseen images, scanned from original negatives and pulled from Life’s vast archive, each page of Let’s Dance reflects an influential era, important dance style, premiere dancer, legendary choreographer, or glamorous star—sometimes all in a single frame. title: Supermedium exhibition at Manchester archive explores past and future of animation
summary: Slip through layers of celluloid animation into an exhibition that asks what it means to animate: to bring life to human-scale animatronics, or to a digital avatar crossing candy-coloured landscapes. Supermedium will showcase commissions and existing work by Kelan Andrews and Petra Szemán, alongside items from the legendary Manchester animation studio Cosgrove Hall Films Archive. The artists’ new works are developed in dialogue with the archive that is home to items from some of the UK’s most iconic and beloved hand-drawn and stop motion animations - Danger Mouse (1981-92) The BFG (1989), The Wind in the Willows (1983-90) and Postman Pat (2004 to 2008) to name just a few. Both artists blur physical and digital realms, working across video, sculpture, claymation, digital animation, augmented reality, and animatronics. title: MMCA Seoul opens largest solo exhibition of Do Ho Suh to date
summary: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea presents a large-scale solo exhibition of Do Ho Suh, a key figure in Korean contemporary art, at MMCA Seoul from Thursday, 27 August 2026, through Tuesday, 9 February 2027. The exhibition is organized to offer a comprehensive survey of the artist’s practice, which has continually expanded in scope over four decades, establishing a distinctive presence both in Korea and on the international stage. It is the largest exhibition of Suh’s work to date. Do Ho Suh (b. 1962) has constructed a distinct artistic world through his inquiry into fundamental questions of the individual and the community, home and displacement, and memory and identity. Based on his experiences of growing up in Seoul and living in the United States and Europe, Suh explores the relationship between home, architecture, the body, and space through diverse media, including sculpture, installation, drawing, and video. title: New Museum to premiere new site-specific commission by Ho Tzu Nyen
summary: On September 24, 2026, the New Museum will debut a new site-specific commission by Ho Tzu Nyen (b. 1976, Singapore; lives and works in Singapore) whose work across film, video, performance, and multimedia installation investigates the plurality of cultural identities across Southeast Asia. Presented in partnership with Hyundai Motor Company as part of the Hyundai Translocal Series: Ho Tzu Nyen, P for Power: Up Down (2026) will premiere at the New Museum, followed later in October by P for Power: Double Life of P (2026) at the Ulsan Art Museum in Ulsan, Korea. Together, the two iterations explore the multiple meanings of power, from political and technological systems to more fluid notions of endurance, transformation, and agency. title: Esther Schipper Seoul presents Simon Fujiwara's first solo show in South Korea
summary: Esther Schipper Seoul announced Who Lived Happily Ever After?, Simon Fujiwara’s first solo exhibition in our Seoul location and the artist’s fourth with the gallery. On view will be new paintings from the artist’s body of work featuring his original cartoon figure Who the Bær – a cartoon bear in constant search for an identity, transforming endlessly into different styles, characters and tropes. For this exhibition, Fujiwara takes Who into the world of myths and fairytales. The works will be presented within a series of themed rooms with differently colored walls. From Hero to Princess, Who transforms into some of our most beloved and archaic cultural figures and characters. title: DC Moore Gallery presents Katia Santibañez solo exhibition And Yet Again
summary: DC Moore Gallery will present And Yet Again, a solo exhibition of new paintings and works on paper by Katia Santibañez. The visual impact of Santibañez’s abstract paintings is immediate, felt simultaneously in the vibrant color combinations on the canvas and also in the intensity of the repeated forms throughout each work. These new paintings mark the artist’s continuing exploration of structure and order within the framework of the grid, which first appeared in her paintings in 2007. The internal logic and thoughtful decision making inherent to Santibañez’s practice is profound in today’s world that moves at warp speed, with endless information available in seconds at the touch of a button. The steady and precise progression of this work requires the artist’s patience and focus, and in turn asks that of the viewer, not only to look, but to intentionally see. Santibañez’s work begins

title: Thaddaeus Ropac Seoul presents Per Mano, a posthumous Georg Baselitz exhibition
summary: Thaddaeus Ropac Seoul presents Per Mano, an exhibition conceived in close collaboration with Georg Baselitz before his passing in April 2026. The show pays homage to the late artist’s prodigious oeuvre through two series of monotype paintings that epitomise the final decade of his practice: the Schatten (2020) and the Darkness Goldness works (2019), never before seen in Korea. It also marks the first time Georg Baselitz’s Schatten will be showcased since his exhibitions at the Sakıp Sabancı Museum, Istanbul (2024) and the Museo de Bellas Artes de Bilbao (2025). Both series reveal the artist’s sustained, eminently sensitive engagement with mortality since the seminal Avignon cycle he presented at the 56th Venice Biennale curated by Okwui Enwezor in 2015. title: New York MTA pays tribute to artist Yayoi Kusama following her death at 97
summary: The Metropolitan Transportation Authority celebrates the life and legacy of the internationally recognized artist Yayoi Kusama, who died on August 14, 2026, in Japan at the age of 97, three years after the MTA unveiled one of her final public artworks at the opening of Grand Central Madison. The artwork, A Message of Love, Directly from My Heart unto the Universe, is a permanent glass mosaic located on the Madison Concourse of Grand Central, between 46th and 47th streets. The vibrant, 120-foot public art installation was commissioned by MTA Arts & Design and the Long Island Railroad and was unveiled to the public in early 2023 with the opening of Grand Central Madison. title: The Ellis-Beauregard Foundation announces 2026 Visual Arts Awardee
summary: The Ellis-Beauregard Foundation announced the recipient of it’s $50,000. 2026 Visual Arts Award. The vision of the Ellis-Beauregard Foundation is to encourage, expand, and sustain the courageous and imaginative dialogue that is fundamental to the arts. The Ellis-Beauregard Foundation celebrates the value of art to transcend cultures and connect with communities. Through its programs, the Foundation supports the exploration of the common ground that art occupies, the way it engages people, and its ability to reveal our shared human experience. title: Gallery Wendi Norris presents Marie Wilson's New York debut at Independent 20th Century
summary: Gallery Wendi Norris will present a selection of paintings and works on paper by the American Surrealist artist Marie Wilson at Independent 20th Century. This marks Wilson’s debut exhibition in New York, as well as the first time many of these works will be on view in the United States. Marie Wilson (1922, Cedarville, CA – 2017, Athens, Greece) produced a revelatory and singular body of work. Her practice was rooted equally in the cultural and spiritual milieu of Northern California and the San Francisco Bay Area of her youth, and in the intellectual currents of European Surrealism, which she experienced while living and working among the movement’s central figures in the 1950s. Over the course of six decades, she created oil paintings, drawings in ink and pencil, lithographs, and ceramics of biomorphic and geometric forms, ranging from semi-abstract arrangements to the exactingly symmetrical compositions of her later period. title: Totally Thames festival returns with over 80 events across London
summary: Totally Thames festival has unveiled its second wave of programming for 2026, presenting a month-long celebration of the River Thames as a place of culture, heritage and environmental connection. Throughout September, audiences can discover immersive performances, free family events and community celebrations, in locations ranging from historic ships and riverside landmarks to hidden tunnels and public spaces. The programme invites Londoners and London’s visitors to experience the Thames as a living landscape shaped by the communities, histories and creativity that continue to define the city. Running throughout September, Culture Cargo (1st – 30th September) transforms the historic sailing barge Raybel into a floating cultural venue as it journeys from the Thames Estuary into central London. title: Marian Goodman Gallery highlights intimate works by French artist Annette Messager
summary: Marian Goodman Gallery is presenting ‘Histoires des oreillers,’ an In Focus Presentation dedicated to Annette Messager. The selection of works features historic and iconic works, some of which are rarely shown to the public. While the exhibition at the Musée de la Chasse et de la Nature in Paris celebrates animality in her work, this new presentation unveils narratives centered on romantic imagery and intimate secrets. It showcases the mischievous spirit and unconventional materials that have characterized the artist’s work since her early years. The works highlight, amongst other things, her penchant for repurposing everyday objects, as illustrated by Histoire des oreillers I (1995–1996) and Les Amoureux (2016); her fondness for wordplay in Les Lignes de la main (1988), Mes Ouvrages (Tolérance) (1988–1989) and Spleen (2025), and her exploration

title: Antiques & Garden Show of Nashville returns January 8-10, 2027
summary: Antiques & Garden Show of Nashville, a benefit for Cheekwood Estate & Gardens and Economic Club of Nashville (ECON) Charities, presented by Northern Trust, announced "Timeless: Living a Collected Life" as the theme for the 2027 Show, returning to Music City Center Jan. 8–10, 2027. The theme celebrates collected spaces, treasured heirlooms and the stories behind the objects that make a house a home. Tickets will go on sale tomorrow, Aug. 28 at antiquesandgardenshow.com. The 2027 Show marks the event's 37th year as the nation's longest-running, largest and most respected event of its kind. Each year, more than 17,000 attendees experience over 150 antiques, art and horticulture exhibitors, immersive garden showcases, educational lectures and special events, all benefiting Cheekwood Estate & Gardens and ECON Charities.

title: Portuguese artist João Maria Gusmão opens analogue film installation at Zachęta
summary: Can film change the way we perceive reality? Following the White Tiger, an exhibition by Portuguese artist João Maria Gusmão presented at Zachęta – National Gallery of Art, invites visitors into the world of analogue cinema. The exhibition comprises a multichannel installation of the artist’s latest 16 mm films, created especially for the exhibition. The project explores the relationship between moving images and reality, encouraging reflection on how film shapes our experience of the world. Following the White Tiger is on view from 28 August to 2 November 2026. Drawing on everyday situations and urban landscapes, Gusmão transforms seemingly ordinary scenes into poetic reflections on perception, technology, and the act of looking. title: Kunstverein Aughrim details upcoming autumn programme including symposium and exhibition
summary: Kunstverein Aughrim presents the closing event of Vaari Claffey’s major public programme, The Clearing. Coming to life through an exhibition, nobody ever brings anything small into a bar at Kunstverein Aughrim; a live event, Fly Specks, at Aughrim’s Craic in the Granite Music & Arts Festival; and a performance and screening programme, Buried with the Machine, at The Courthouse Arts Centre, Tinahely, The Clearing has marked a summer-long pitstop in Claffey’s actively artistic curatorial practice. Through a series of new commissions developed in close collaboration with artists, and supported by an Arts Council Project Award, Claffey has devised encounters that invite pause for reflection, before continuing on possible and unknowable journeys ahead. title: Jane Jin Kaisen opens site-specific exhibition at Pulverturm Oldenburg
summary: The Haus for Media Art Oldenburg presents a solo exhibition by Danish-Korean artist Jane Jin Kaisen within the historic walls of the Pulverturm—a site-specific installation of three poetic, immersive video works based on meticulous historical research. Offering (2023) and Wreckage (2024) are joined by a newly produced third work, created to echo the tower’s architecture. As a descendant of Jeju Island’s haenyeo (sea women) divers, celebrated for their ability to remain deep underwater without equipment, Kaisen has spent more than fifteen years researching their history through the lens of Korea’s colonial past. The sea becomes both threat and promise—an archive of memory, and a vessel of matrilineal knowledge. title: Galerie Maria Wettergren presents Hyejeong Ko solo exhibition Silver Shadows
summary: Galerie Maria Wettergren will present Silver Shadows, an exhibition by South Korean artist Hyejeong Ko, from September 4 to October 31, 2026. Winner of several awards, including the Boghossian Foundation Prize in 2025, the Homo Faber Award in 2024, and the Grand Prize at the Cheongju International Craft Competition in 2023, the artist creates sculptures in sterling silver, inspired by the natural landscapes of her birthplace, the volcanic island of Jeju. Hyejeong Ko transforms her perception of organic forms found in nature—dandelions, pebbles, sea urchins, and streams—into shimmering, ethereal sculptures. Yet rather than simply imitating natural forms, her works are inspired by the dynamics of natural phenomena, expressed through the Taoist philosophy of Wu Wei—an effortless action and harmony with the natural course of things. title: Zander Galerie presents Torn Skies, a survey of paintings by Joe Goode
summary: Zander Galerie is presenting Torn Skies, an exhibition of paintings and works on paper by American artist Joe Goode (1937–2025). Covering more than three decades, the exhibition brings together key works from some of the artist’s most significant bodies of work. One would expect a serial practice to help artists to compartmentalize their subjects, allowing each to be treated independently of the others. What is surprising, then, is the abiding centrality of a single notion in the work of Joe Goode, who is unmistakably a serial painter. Perhaps even more important than its recurrence is the substance of this central notion itself: the sky. Vast, all-encompassing, total, everything but central in a localized, nuclear fashion: on the contrary, the sky extends toward omnipresence, both in the real world and throughout Goode’s formal development. title: Ragnar Kjartansson" Politics of the Obvious to open at Buffalo AKG Art Museum
summary: Ragnar Kjartansson works across performance, music, and image to create shared emotional experiences from otherwise commonplace or familiar scenes. Politics of the Obvious is one of the celebrated Icelandic artist’s most ambitious ever exhibitions in the United States and half of the works are making their American museum debut at the Buffalo AKG. The exhibition centers on a series of deceptively simple refrains, clichés, and truisms. In six immersive installations made over more than two decades, Kjartansson transforms such familiar phrases or gestures into experiences that become altogether strange, provocative, and powerfully moving. title: Alfonso Artiaco presents Gianmarco Biele solo exhibition storie del giardino
summary: Alfonso Artiaco will present storie del giardino, Gianmarco Biele’s first solo exhibition with the gallery, curated by Mario Francesco Simeone. The exhibition will open on September 3, 2026 at 7:00 pm, in the presence of the artist. Bringing together nine new paintings and a sculptural intervention, the exhibition is the outcome of an extensive body of research centered on the garden. Long at the core of Biele’s practice, the garden emerges as a subject of profound symbolic complexity – an ancestral topos through which to reflect on the relationship between human beings and an ever-changing universe, between what belongs entirely to nature and what is shaped by cultural construction. title: Richard Lewer's Steve begins national tour in regional South Australia
summary: The National Gallery of Australia will take a compelling work by Richard Lewer exploring memory and the impact of dementia on family on a three-year tour to communities across Australia. Following its presentation at the National Gallery in Kamberri/Canberra, Richard Lewer: Steve opens at Port Pirie Regional Art Gallery, SA on 28 August 2026. The National Gallery Touring Exhibition will then travel to Redcliffe Art Gallery, Qld; Maitland Regional Art Gallery, NSW; Tweed Regional Gallery, NSW; Manningham Art Gallery, Vic; John Curtin Gallery, WA; and Ngununggula, NSW. Naarm/Melbourne-based Lewer is a visual storyteller with a longstanding interest in the relationship between art and health, well known for his paintings, drawings and moving image works that focus on the complexities of the human condition.
